display.title: Episode 213: The Ten Wedding Gifts, Chapter 4 (Parshas Tetzaveh)
display.summary_short: The golden bells of Aharon's robe teach children to say brachos out loud; the Baal Shem Tov's ten gifts come true in 'The Ten Wedding Gifts'; and Mitzvah Time explains shemos.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in the week of Parshas Tetzaveh 5746. Uncle Yossi explains why we learn a part of the weekly sedra with Rashi every day, so we are ready by Shabbos and show that the Torah is our life. From Tuesday's portion he describes the golden bells on Aharon HaKohen's robe, whose sound was heard as he entered the holy place: there is a time for children to be quiet and not interrupt, but when saying a brachah, davening or benching, our voices should be heard, like sweet music to Hashem. After the Hakochainik march for Adar, a young member who recruits friends to Tzivos Hashem leads the Shema. 'The Ten Wedding Gifts' concludes: the boy Avraham and Sarah sheltered is the only son of a poritz. Avraham refuses a reward, saying he only did what the Torah teaches, but the poritz holds a banquet and gives them the town park, another poritz gives the lumberyard, and so on until all ten gifts promised by the Baal Shem Tov's students are fulfilled. In Mitzvah Time, Uncle Yossi explains shemos: worn-out holy books and pages go into a shemos box and are buried, never thrown out or burned.
display.lesson: Let your voice be heard when you talk to Hashem; and Hashem rewards kindness in full, just as the tzaddik promised.
